genZNote: Sets up lifelong latency in B cells and, decades later, gets linked to cancers most acute viruses would never touch.

morphology.shape: Spherical, enveloped virion with icosahedral capsid

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human B lymphocytes and oropharyngeal epithelium; establishes lifelong latency in memory B cells
habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human pathogen, extremely widespread — most adults worldwide are infected
habitat.reservoir: Infected humans, often asymptomatic intermittent oral shedders

identificationClues: Heterophile antibody (Monospot) test is the classic rapid screening test, though it can be falsely negative early in illness or in young children
Atypical (reactive) lymphocytes on peripheral blood smear support the diagnosis
EBV-specific serology (VCA IgM/IgG, EBNA) confirms and can stage the timing of infection when the heterophile test is negative or ambiguous
Classic triad of fever, pharyngitis, and lymphadenopathy, often with splenomegaly

diseases: Associated with several malignancies, including Burkitt lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and some Hodgkin lymphomas
Post-transplant lymphoproliferative disease in immunosuppressed transplant recipients
clinicalImportance.transmission: Saliva ("kissing disease") primarily; less commonly through blood transfusion, organ transplantation, or sexual contact
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common human viruses worldwide — most people are infected at some point, often asymptomatically in early childhood, with symptomatic mononucleosis more typical when primary infection occurs during adolescence or young adulthood
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Splenomegaly is a clinically important finding — contact sports/activities with abdominal trauma risk are typically restricted for several weeks due to the risk of splenic rupture

examFacts.importantDisease: Infectious mononucleosis; associated with Burkitt lymphoma and nasopharyngeal carcinoma
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Established lifelong B-cell latency links it to several distinct malignancies, unlike most acute viral infections
